1. For example, claude code may support enterprise version (api key based)? 
2. Also codex support other variants like azure api key etc? 

Can you do a proper search and then
1. list all the different environment setup support for claude code / codex apps 
2. we can try update the https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/resolve-agent-provider/resolve-provider.sh script ?

@sepo-agent /answer

comments.body:
I checked #233 and did not find a linked parent/tracking issue or comments.

For this `/answer` run I’m staying in plan-only mode. Short version: yes, Sepo should support more credential shapes, but updating only [`resolve-provider.sh`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/resolve-agent-provider/resolve-provider.sh#L39-L45) is not enough. The workflow also needs to pass those secrets into the runtime via [`resolve-agent-provider/action.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/resolve-agent-provider/action.yml#L16-L23), [`run-agent-task/action.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L294-L302), and [`run.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/run.ts#L256-L273).

**Current Sepo Behavior**

- Auto-detects Codex only from `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- Auto-detects Claude only from `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.
- Explicit `AGENT_DEFAULT_PROVIDER=codex|claude` already works without matching repo secrets, mainly for self-hosted runners with local auth.
- Runtime only forwards `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` to the agent process.

**Claude Code Supported Auth/Env Setups**

Based on current official Claude Code docs:

- Claude.ai subscription auth: `/login` for Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise.
- CI subscription auth: `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, generated via `claude setup-token`.
- Direct Anthropic API key: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- Bearer/proxy auth: `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`.
- Dynamic credentials: `apiKeyHelper` plus optional `CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS`.
- Enterprise/team managed settings: managed `settings.json`/policy layers, including server-managed and OS/MDM/file-based managed settings.
- Amazon Bedrock: `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1`, `AWS_REGION`, AWS SDK credential chain or `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`.
- Claude Platform on AWS: `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS=1`, `ANTHROPIC_AWS_WORKSPACE_ID`, `AWS_REGION`, plus AWS credentials or `ANTHROPIC_AWS_API_KEY`.
- Google Vertex AI: `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1`, `CLOUD_ML_REGION`, `ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID`, plus ADC / `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`.
- Microsoft Foundry/Azure: `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1`, `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_RESOURCE` or `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL`, plus `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY` or Azure default credentials.
- LLM gateways/proxies: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, optional `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`, gateway model discovery flags.

Sources: [Claude auth](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication), [Claude env vars](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars), [Bedrock](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock), [Claude Platform on AWS](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-platform-on-aws), [Vertex](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai), [Foundry](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/microsoft-foundry), [LLM gateway](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway).

**Codex Supported Auth/Env Setups**

Based on current official Codex docs:

- ChatGPT account auth: `codex login`, including Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, Enterprise plans.
- CI/API-key auth: official non-interactive docs now call out `CODEX_API_KEY` for `codex exec`; Sepo currently uses `OPENAI_API_KEY`, so I would support both for compatibility.
- Codex GitHub Action: uses an `openai-api-key` input backed by a secret such as `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- Custom/OpenAI-compatible providers: `~/.codex/config.toml` or project `.codex/config.toml` with `[model_providers.<id>]`, `base_url`, `env_key`, `wire_api`, headers, or command-backed auth.
- Azure OpenAI: Codex supports an Azure provider config using `env_key = "AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY"`, Azure base URL, `api-version` query param, and `wire_api = "responses"`. Important: `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY` alone is not enough; Codex still needs provider config.
- Built-in Amazon Bedrock provider: `model_provider = "amazon-bedrock"` plus AWS profile/region/credential chain.
- Data residency / proxy: `openai_base_url` for the built-in OpenAI provider, or a custom provider for gateways.
- Local OSS mode: Ollama / LM Studio via `--oss` and config.

Sources: [Codex non-interactive auth](https://developers.openai.com/codex/noninteractive), [Codex config/custom providers](https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-advanced), [Codex GitHub Action](https://developers.openai.com/codex/github-action), [Codex repo README](https://github.com/openai/codex).

**Recommended Implementation**

1. Keep provider choices as `auto|codex|claude`; do not split into `claude-bedrock`, `codex-azure`, etc. Those are credential/config variants of the same CLI providers.
2. Add fixed, explicit inputs to `resolve-agent-provider` for known readiness signals:
   - Codex: `codex_api_key`, `openai_api_key`, `azure_openai_api_key`.
   - Claude: `claude_oauth_token`, `anthropic_api_key`, `anthropic_auth_token`, `anthropic_aws_api_key`, `aws_bearer_token_bedrock`, `anthropic_foundry_api_key`, plus provider activation/config vars where needed.
3. Update `resolve-provider.sh` so `auto` considers these additional signals, while keeping Codex-first behavior when both are configured.
4. Update `run-agent-task` and `run.ts` to forward the same fixed env vars to `acpx`.
5. Update workflow call sites to wire repo secrets explicitly. Do not pass arbitrary secrets wholesale.
6. Update docs and onboarding output so setup no longer says only `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.
7. Add resolver tests for:
   - `CODEX_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`
   - `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY` with Codex
   - `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
   - `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`
   - `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`
   - Bedrock / Foundry / AWS workspace API-key cases
   - deterministic Codex-first tie behavior

One design question before coding: should Sepo only detect/pass these env vars and assume provider-specific config already exists, or should Sepo also generate `.codex/config.toml` / Claude settings for cases like Azure OpenAI and gateways? My recommendation for the first PR is detection + fixed env forwarding + docs, leaving config generation for a separate issue because it has more policy/security surface.

@sepo-agent /answer 

also how do we set models and reasoning effort in the current repo?

Currently Sepo separates three things:

1. **Provider selection**: `codex` vs `claude`
2. **Reasoning effort**: `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, etc.
3. **Actual model ID**: mostly left to the underlying Codex/Claude CLI config

Provider is configurable today via repo variable `AGENT_DEFAULT_PROVIDER`, documented in [`configuration-list.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/customization/configuration-list.md#L7-L10). Valid values are:

```text
auto
codex
claude
```

`auto` detects configured secrets and prefers Codex when both are present. Route-specific provider overrides are possible by editing the relevant workflow’s `resolve-agent-provider` step, per [`configuration-list.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/customization/configuration-list.md#L34).

Reasoning effort is wired through [`run-agent-task`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L19-L26) as the `reasoning_effort` input. The runtime then maps that into:

- `MODEL_REASONING_EFFORT`
- `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`
- Codex persistent-session `thought_level`

See [`run.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/run.ts#L256-L273), [`run.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/run.ts#L521-L531), and [`acpx-adapter.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/acpx-adapter.ts#L285-L291).

Current hardcoded reasoning values include:

- `/answer`: `high` in [`agent-router.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L320-L344)
- `/implement`: effectively `xhigh`, via the `run-agent-task` default; the workflow also has `MODEL_REASONING_EFFORT: xhigh` in [`agent-implement.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-implement.yml#L130-L134)
- `/fix-pr`: effectively `xhigh`, similarly in [`agent-fix-pr.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-fix-pr.yml#L111-L187)
- review matrix: Claude uses `max`, Codex uses `xhigh` in [`agent-review.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L138-L148)
- review synthesis: `max` for Claude, `xhigh` for Codex in [`agent-review.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L320-L326)
- project/daily/memory tasks are mostly `medium`; orchestrator/rubrics/skill paths are mostly `high`

Actual **model ID** is not centrally configurable in Sepo today. There is no repo variable like `AGENT_MODEL`, `CODEX_MODEL`, or `CLAUDE_MODEL`. Sepo invokes `acpx` with the selected agent and effort; model choice comes from the underlying Codex/Claude CLI defaults or local runner config.

So today, to change models you would use provider-native config on the runner, for example Codex/Claude config files or env vars supported by those CLIs. To make this reproducible in GitHub-hosted Actions, we should add first-class Sepo config such as:

```text
AGENT_CODEX_MODEL
AGENT_CLAUDE_MODEL
AGENT_REASONING_EFFORT_DEFAULT
AGENT_REASONING_EFFORT_BY_ROUTE
```

and then plumb those through `run-agent-task` / `run.ts` / `acpx-adapter.ts`, similar to how reasoning effort is already handled.

@sepo-agent /answer 

But also can we set via repo environment variables (so this avoids us manually setting things)?

Yes, but not fully today.

GitHub repo variables only affect a workflow when the workflow explicitly reads `vars.NAME`. Current Sepo already does that for things like `AGENT_DEFAULT_PROVIDER`, `AGENT_RUNS_ON`, memory/rubrics refs, timeout policy, etc. See [`configuration-list.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/customization/configuration-list.md#L3-L32).

For **models and reasoning effort**, current state is:

- Provider can be set with repo variable `AGENT_DEFAULT_PROVIDER=auto|codex|claude`.
- Reasoning effort is mostly hardcoded in workflow YAML, for example `/answer` uses `high` in [`agent-router.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L320-L344).
- The shared action supports a `reasoning_effort` input with default `xhigh` in [`run-agent-task/action.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L19-L26).
- The runtime forwards that into `MODEL_REASONING_EFFORT` / `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` in [`run.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/run.ts#L256-L274).
- There is no current repo variable for model ID, like `AGENT_CODEX_MODEL` or `AGENT_CLAUDE_MODEL`.

So the answer is:

- **Reasoning effort can be repo-variable controlled with a small workflow change.**
- **Model ID needs a small runtime/action change, because Sepo currently does not pass a model setting through centrally.**

A practical first pass would be:

```yaml
reasoning_effort: ${{ vars.AGENT_REASONING_EFFORT_ANSWER || 'high' }}
```

and similar route-specific vars:

```text
AGENT_REASONING_EFFORT_DEFAULT=xhigh
AGENT_REASONING_EFFORT_ANSWER=high
AGENT_REASONING_EFFORT_DISPATCH=medium
AGENT_REASONING_EFFORT_IMPLEMENT=xhigh
AGENT_REASONING_EFFORT_FIX_PR=xhigh
AGENT_REASONING_EFFORT_ORCHESTRATOR=high
AGENT_REASONING_EFFORT_REVIEW_CODEX=xhigh
AGENT_REASONING_EFFORT_REVIEW_CLAUDE=max
```

For models, I’d add explicit repo vars/secrets support rather than relying on manual runner config:

```text
AGENT_CODEX_MODEL=...
AGENT_CLAUDE_MODEL=...
AGENT_CODEX_MODEL_PROVIDER=...
AGENT_CLAUDE_MODEL_PROVIDER=...
```

Then plumb those through:

1. `.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml` inputs
2. workflow `with:` blocks using `vars.AGENT_CODEX_MODEL`, `vars.AGENT_CLAUDE_MODEL`, etc.
3. `.agent/src/run.ts` shared env construction
4. `.agent/src/acpx-adapter.ts` provider/session setup, if `acpx` requires model setting commands rather than env-only config
5. docs/tests

I’d probably prefer a JSON policy long-term to avoid too many vars:

```json
{
  "default": { "reasoning_effort": "xhigh" },
  "routes": {
    "answer": { "reasoning_effort": "high" },
    "dispatch": { "reasoning_effort": "medium" }
  },
  "providers": {
    "codex": { "model": "..." },
    "claude": { "model": "..." }
  }
}
```

But for a first implementation, route-specific repo variables are simpler and easier to audit in Actions.

**Sepo implementation finished**

- Branch: `agent/implement-issue-233/codex-26197424768`
- Pull request: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/332

Added direct `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` support for Claude-backed Sepo runs by extending provider resolution, workflow secret plumbing, agent runtime env forwarding, onboarding status, setup guidance, and focused regression tests. Verified with `npm run build`, `GITHUB_OUTPUT=/tmp/sepo-agent-test-output node --test dist/__tests__/resolve-agent-provider.test.js dist/__tests__/onboarding-check-cli.test.js dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js`, and `git diff --check`.

title: More flexible api key setups for codex and claude
